title: Right Front Wheel Speed Sensor Supply
plain: The ABS computer sees a problem with the power supply to the right front wheel speed sensor. Some makers, GM especially, use C0 numbers with their own meanings, so confirm with a make-specific lookup. On many GM vehicles, C0035 is used for the left front wheel speed sensor circuit.
symptoms: ABS, traction control or stability light on
ABS may not work on slippery roads
Cruise control or speedometer may act up on some vehicles

causes.name: Damaged or chafed sensor wire near the wheel
Corroded connector at the sensor
Failed wheel speed sensor
ABS module fault (rare)

checks: Look at the sensor wire for damage from road debris or suspension movement
Check sensor supply voltage at the connector
Compare all four wheel speeds in live data while driving slowly
fix: Usually a wiring repair or a new wheel speed sensor.
drive: Normal brakes usually still work, but ABS and stability control may not. Leave extra stopping distance, brake gently on wet or icy roads, and get it checked in the next few days.

title: Right Rear Wheel Speed Sensor
plain: The ABS computer has a problem with the right rear wheel speed sensor. Some makers, GM especially, use C0 numbers with their own meanings, so confirm with a make-specific lookup.
symptoms: ABS, traction control or stability light on
ABS may not work on slippery roads
Cruise control or speedometer may act up on some vehicles

causes.name: Damaged or dirty wheel speed sensor
Broken or chafed sensor wire near the wheel
Rusted, cracked or debris-covered tone ring
Worn wheel bearing with excess play
ABS module fault (rare)

checks: Look at the right rear sensor wire for damage
Compare all four wheel speeds in live data while driving slowly
Clean rust or debris off the sensor tip and tone ring
fix: Usually a new wheel speed sensor or wiring repair; sometimes a wheel bearing or hub with a built-in tone ring.
drive: Normal brakes usually still work, but ABS and stability control may not. Leave extra stopping distance, brake gently on wet or icy roads, and get it checked in the next few days.

title: Brake Pedal Switch "A"
plain: The brake computer has a problem with the brake pedal switch "A", which tells the car's computers when you press the brake. Some makers, GM especially, use C0 numbers with their own meanings, so confirm with a make-specific lookup. On many GM vehicles, C0040 is used for the right front wheel speed sensor circuit.
symptoms: ABS, traction or stability light on
Brake lights may stay on or not come on
Cruise control may not work; the shifter may stick in Park

causes.name: Faulty or out-of-adjustment brake pedal switch
Wiring or connector problem at the switch
Blown brake light fuse

checks: Have a helper check that the brake lights come on and go off with the pedal
Check the switch adjustment and connector
Watch the switch signal in live data
fix: Usually a new or adjusted brake pedal switch.

title: Brake Pedal Switch "B"
plain: The brake computer has a problem with the brake pedal switch "B", a second signal that tells the car's computers when you press the brake. Some makers, GM especially, use C0 numbers with their own meanings, so confirm with a make-specific lookup.
symptoms: ABS, traction or stability light on
Brake lights may stay on or not come on
Cruise control may not work

causes.name: Faulty or out-of-adjustment brake pedal switch
Wiring or connector problem at the switch
Blown fuse

checks: Have a helper check that the brake lights come on and go off with the pedal
Check the switch adjustment and connector
Compare switch A and B signals in live data
fix: Usually a new or adjusted brake pedal switch.

title: Brake Pressure Sensor "B"
plain: The brake computer has a problem with brake pressure sensor "B", which measures how hard the brakes are being applied. Some makers, GM especially, use C0 numbers with their own meanings, so confirm with a make-specific lookup. On many GM vehicles, C0045 is used for the left rear wheel speed sensor circuit.
symptoms: ABS, traction or stability light on
Stability control or brake assist may not work
Brake pedal may feel different on some vehicles

causes.name: Faulty brake pressure sensor (often in the ABS unit)
Wiring or connector problem
Low brake fluid
ABS module fault

checks: Check the brake fluid level
Compare pressure sensor readings with pedal application in live data
Check the sensor connector and wiring
fix: Often a new pressure sensor or ABS unit, depending on the design.
drive: Normal brakes usually still work, but ABS and stability control may not. Leave extra stopping distance, brake gently on wet or icy roads, and get it checked in the next few days.

title: 4WD/AWD Rear Differential Unit Actuator "A"
plain: The all-wheel-drive computer has a problem with the actuator in the rear drive unit, the part that sends power to the rear wheels.
symptoms: Service AWD or 4WD message
All-wheel drive not working
Binding or hopping in tight turns on some vehicles

causes.name: Failed rear drive unit actuator or clutch
Wiring or connector problem at the rear drive unit
Low or worn rear drive unit fluid
Software problem that an update may fix

checks: Check the rear drive unit connector and wiring
Check the rear drive unit fluid
Ask the dealer about bulletins or software updates (the Bulletins page explains what a bulletin is)
fix: Depends on the test: often a software update, actuator or rear drive unit repair.
drive: The car usually still drives in front-wheel drive. Take extra care on snow, ice or mud until it's fixed. If you feel binding, hopping or hear grinding in tight turns, get it checked soon.

title: VIN Not Programmed or Incompatible - BSCM
plain: The brake system control module doesn't have the right vehicle ID (VIN) stored. This usually happens after the module was replaced or reprogrammed.
symptoms: ABS, traction or stability light on
ABS and stability control may be turned off

causes.name: Brake module replaced or reprogrammed without the VIN set up
Wrong or used module installed
Programming that didn't finish

checks: Ask whether the brake module was recently replaced
Read the VIN stored in each module with a scan tool
Have the module programmed with the dealer's or a capable shop's tool
fix: Program the brake module with the correct VIN, or install the correct module.
drive: Normal brakes usually still work, but ABS and stability control may not. Leave extra stopping distance, brake gently on wet or icy roads, and get it checked in the next few days.

title: Vacuum Sensor A/B Correlation
plain: The two signals from the brake booster vacuum sensor don't agree. The brake booster uses vacuum to make the brake pedal easier to push. Some makers, GM especially, use C0 numbers with their own meanings, so confirm with a make-specific lookup.
symptoms: ABS, stability or brake warning light
Brake assist may not work
Brake pedal may feel harder on some vehicles

causes.name: Faulty brake booster vacuum sensor
Wiring or connector problem
Vacuum leak or failing vacuum pump

checks: Check the brake booster vacuum hose and check valve
Compare the two sensor signals in live data
Check the sensor connector and wiring
fix: Usually a new vacuum sensor or wiring repair; a vacuum leak or pump if tests show low vacuum.
